title: Gitignore
summary: Explains why and how to keep files out of Git using a .gitignore file: secrets, OS and editor settings, and generated folders such as node_modules. Demonstrates ignoring individual files and patterns, undoing an accidental git add with git rm --cached, and starting a Node project from GitHub's pre-made .gitignore template.

concepts.heading: What should not be committed
points: Secrets: passwords, API keys, cloud credentials. Once pushed to a public remote they can be harvested almost immediately, with real financial damage possible.

Personal or machine-specific files: editor settings, OS metadata such as macOS .DS_Store (a hidden file storing things like icon arrangement in a folder). They are useless to collaborators and clutter the repository.
(Extra) Generated or downloadable content such as node_modules, build output and logs; these can be recreated with npm install or a build.

concepts.heading: Creating and writing .gitignore
points: Create a plain file named exactly .gitignore (leading dot, lowercase) in the project root, e.g. with touch .gitignore. It is hidden, so use ls -a to see it. Git looks for this exact name.
One pattern per line. To ignore a single file, write its name exactly, matching case: .DS_Store, secrets.txt.
A line starting with # is a comment.
Wildcards: *.txt ignores every file ending in .txt anywhere under the repository. Use with care, since it will exclude files you actually want.
(Extra) A trailing slash such as logs/ matches directories; a leading ! re-includes a path that an earlier rule excluded.
The .gitignore file itself is normally committed so that collaborators share the same rules.

concepts.heading: Demo sequence
points: Project folder with file1.txt, file2.txt, file3.txt and a secrets file, plus a .DS_Store, and an empty .gitignore.
git init, then git add . stages everything; git status shows the unwanted secrets and .DS_Store would be committed.
To undo that staging: git rm --cached -r . removes everything from the staging area (index) while leaving the files on disk; -r makes it recursive. git status then shows nothing staged.
Add .DS_Store and secrets.txt to .gitignore, run git add . again and check git status: only .gitignore and the three file1-3 files are staged; the ignored ones no longer appear.
Committing and pushing now includes only those four files.

concepts.heading: Templates for Node projects
points: GitHub maintains a public repository named gitignore (under the github organisation) with ready-made templates per language and framework. The Node template already covers node_modules, logs, environment files and similar.
Copy the template contents into your .gitignore and add your own extras, for instance a '# Project-wide' comment followed by .DS_Store.
Flow shown: new Node project, npm install, create .gitignore with the template, then git init, git add ., git status, git commit -m 'Initial commit'.
Use .gitignore for API keys and other sensitive data before the first commit; list the files holding them (for instance .env).

concepts.heading: Important limitation
points: (Extra) .gitignore only affects untracked files. A file that was already committed stays tracked and in history after you add it to .gitignore; remove it from tracking with git rm --cached <file>. A secret that was ever pushed should be treated as leaked and rotated, because it still exists in history.

code_examples.caption: Ignoring files in a fresh project
code_examples.code:
cd ~/Desktop/Project
touch .gitignore
ls -a                  # .gitignore and .DS_Store visible
git init
git add .              # oops: secrets.txt and .DS_Store got staged
git status
git rm --cached -r .   # unstage everything (files stay on disk)
# edit .gitignore, then:
git add .
git status             # secrets and .DS_Store no longer listed
git commit -m "Initial commit"

pitfalls: Wrong name or case (gitignore, .Gitignore); Git silently ignores it.
Adding a file to .gitignore after it was committed or staged; it keeps being tracked until removed with git rm --cached.
Overly broad wildcards like *.txt that exclude files you meant to keep.
Pushing secrets to a public repository before setting up .gitignore.
(Extra) git rm --cached -r . without a path argument unstages everything; it does not delete files from disk.

gaps_and_ideas: Add to the proposed Git lesson series a .gitignore task: given a file list in a simulated repo, write patterns so git status shows only the intended files.
Demo idea: a pattern tester where the learner types .gitignore lines and sees which sample paths (node_modules/, .env, secrets.txt, app.log, notes.txt) are ignored or tracked.
Concept check: what happens if you add a file to .gitignore after committing it.
